evidence: Current sources read/edited and cached Java/JOML class bytes decoded as data only; no classes loaded, compilation, syntax check, tests, GPU calls, game execution or process inspection

javaReference.centroids: MeshData.decodeQuadCentroids reads float XYZ at vertices 0/2, adds each pair and divides by float 2 before storing
javaReference.sort: VertexSorting.lambda$byDistance$0 builds original indices and keys, then IntArrays.mergeSort with comparator lambda$byDistance$1 comparing key[b] against key[a] through Floats.compare
javaReference.perspective: VertexSorting.byDistance captures the origin Vector3fc and invokes its distanceSquared against the centroid
javaReference.joml: JOML 1.10.8 Vector3f.distanceSquared(Vector3fc): origin-centroid per axis; nested Math.fma gives dx*dx+(dy*dy+dz*dz) on the default non-FMA path
javaReference.customFeature: CustomFeatureRenderer.buildGroup walks submits in order and gets the vertex builder for each selected RenderType
javaReference.consolidation: RenderTypeFeatureRenderer.Group.getVertexBuilder reuses the last draw for the same RenderType object only when consecutive geometry can consolidate; getOrAddDraw may otherwise search the first equal PreparedRenderType when the group can reorder and the current submit can consolidate
javaReference.drawCreation: Group.getOrAddDraw captures ProjectionType.vertexSorting only for sortOnUpload types and preserves draw creation order
javaReference.phaseDelivery: SimpleFeatureRenderPhase.sortFeatureInto emits unbatched entries and each HashMap batch using strictlyOrdered=false, not canReorder=false; maybeShuffle can alter collection/batch traversal in debug mode
javaReference.customBatchKey: CustomFeatureRenderer.Submit.batchKey returns its RenderType reference; FeatureSubmits retains each batch's insertion order in ArrayList and traverses batches through HashMap.values
javaReference.dispatcherMerge: PhaseSubmitGrouper.addOrExtendGroup extends the last group when featureType reference and strictlyOrdered match, even across separately emitted texture batches. acceptFeatureGroup ignores empty collections. A newly constructed phase grouper has no last group.
javaReference.strictnessInversion: PreparedGroup.prepare passes strictlyOrdered through unchanged; RenderTypeFeatureRenderer.prepareGroup constructs Group(stagedVertexBuffer, !strictlyOrdered)
javaReference.modelOrdering: TranslucentFeatureRenderPhase orders submits by descending supplied distanceToCameraSq using IntArrays.unstableSort and emits strictlyOrdered=true; this is separate from stable per-draw quad sorting

sourcePort.groupInputs: Ordered feature groups, can_reorder flag, every staged batch, separate render-object/prepared-equality IDs, consolidate flag and explicit sorting policy
sourcePort.identity: Supported named factory calls now carry owned JavaRenderType cache-reference IDs in ARCGEO07, and Plan checks supplied render-object IDs against them (java-render-type-reference-source.json). Remaining prepared-equality and feature identities still require their owning producer; no prepared identity is inferred from pixel/name/material resemblance.
policies: literal orthographic negative Z in the declared sorter coordinate space
sourcePort.stableComparison: Java float comparison including signed zero/canonical NaN ordering; stable ties retain original submit/quad order
sourcePort.groupValidation: Every batch exactly once, including empty batches; reference/prepared identities must have coherent descriptors; reject unknown coordinate space for derived perspective origin
sourcePort.output: Contiguous original index ranges coalesced only within a batch while retaining the computed order
sourcePort.frameOwnership: Plan borrows the exact source Frame; Uploaded exposes immutable frame and buffer-view accessors
sourcePort.newWirePattern: Java writer and native decoder now use exact [0,1,2,2,3,0] rather than a cyclic rotation of the second triangle
sourcePort.softwarePattern: Raster3D submits its second triangle as 2,3,0 before polygon clipping and fan triangulation, matching the wire/native reference primitive order. Previously its 0,2,3 cyclic rotation preserved winding but changed the input anchor for floating-point clipping/interpolation. Pixel equivalence remains unverified.
sourcePort.emptySubmits: Java staging/packet/native decoder preserve zero-vertex batches; they still participate in draw consolidation boundaries
sourcePort.allEmptyUpload: Returns no upload ticket or GPU command; mixed frames retain empty metadata without binding zero-length views
sourcePort.phaseAssembly: FeatureGroup.from_phases consumes ordered PhaseOutput deliveries, merges adjacent matching feature/strictness deliveries within one phase, ignores empty collections and inverts strictly_ordered into can_reorder
sourcePort.assemblyEntry: Geometry.from_phase_outputs performs dispatcher assembly and the existing Plan/material preflight; it does not schedule or execute the live renderer
sourcePort.modelPhase: Phase.translucent_models consumes model boundaries from ARCGEO08 plus explicit owning Java-equivalent view-pose translations and per-batch preparation inputs. Mth left-associated float distance and fastutil 8.5.18 unstable comparator quicksort order entire models, with strictly_ordered=true. Parts preserve their original order and one vertex builder, including when inter-model consolidation is disabled. See java-model-submit-source.json.
sourcePort.modelAtomicity: Plan rejects split/restarted models, later-part-first ordering, changed preparation/sort/consolidation metadata, and nonconsecutive part batches. It reuses the one model vertex builder without conflating that with consolidation across different models.
sourcePort.ownedSimplePhaseProducer: JavaSimplePhases retains actual owned JavaRenderType HashMap keys and Java-style bucket/order lifecycle. ARCGEO09 transports the resulting nonempty simple-phase traversal and epoch. This covers only the port renderer's avatar scope and geometry-collection history, not an independent Java game's hashes or native world ownership.
sourcePort.ownedScopeAssembly: Phase.owned_avatars and Geometry.from_owned_avatar_inputs join the packet's simple-phase output with explicit preparations/feature IDs/model view poses: order 0 solid(0), models(7), custom(8), then order 1 glow(8). Decoder checks complete simple-role coverage, reference bucket contiguity and within-bucket source order. See java-simple-phase-source.json.
sourcePort.phaseRecording: OrderedPhase retains numeric order/phase locations through Geometry group mapping. Plan retains each group's range slice; Pipelines.prepare_groups selects increasing unique groups after complete preflight, and native_avatar_record.record_phase emits only that current phase. Known multi-phase owned geometry is rejected by the legacy whole-frame recording entry. Native wing glint has a separate order 1 model-phase 7 transaction. See native-avatar-phase-recording-source.json.

recording.identityJoin: Plan must borrow this exact Uploaded frame object
recording.preflight: Validate complete constant-slot mapping, material role, projection/tint, descriptors and quad-aligned index ranges before recording commands
recording.rangeEmission: DrawIndexedInstanced uses the ordered first-index/count pairs against owned unchanged index buffers
recording.descriptorHeap: Bound after preflight and retained by Uploaded
recording.laterSubmission: Owning world renderer must still submit and retain pipelines/constants/uploaded resources through its draw fence

limitations: Live world phase ownership/foreign participation, owning feature-reference IDs, prepared-equality IDs and consolidation flags remain unfinished; the supported source-port avatar collector now transports its own simple-phase output through ARCGEO09.

The owned Java collector now supplies its own HashMap traversal/history. Captured Java game identity hashes/foreign cache history and optional debug shuffle remain unavailable. Model-level unstable ordering has a source sorter, but authoritative Java-equivalent view translations still require their owning producer; packet roots and actor positions do not prove this equivalence.
Orthographic coordinate-space equivalence must be established by the adapter; world Z is not assumed equivalent
Whole-world ordering relative to native terrain/translucency remains unverified
Source range emission can require up to one draw per quad; production performance/optimized equivalent index batching are unverified
Nondefault JOML FMA/fast-math modes are not reproduced
Native lightmap/fog/overlay and scene packed-light producers, world/depth joins, draw-fence retirement and presentation integration remain incomplete
